name: The River Café
description: Ruth Rogers' Italian dining room beside the Thames in Hammersmith — wood-fired oven, seasonal produce, a kitchen-garden terrace.
address: Thames Wharf, Rainville Rd, London W6 9HA
tips: Book weeks ahead. The chocolate Nemesis cake is legend.

name: Padella Shoreditch
description: The Shoreditch sister of the beloved pasta counter — reservations accepted, same £10 pappardelle with 8-hour beef shin ragu.
tips: This branch takes reservations. The original Padella on Southwark Street does not.

name: Manteca
description: Chris Leach and David Carter's nose-to-tail Italian in Shoreditch — house-made pasta, dry-aged beef, and house-butchered charcuterie.
tips: The brown-butter tortellini with 60-month Parmesan is extraordinary.

name: Trullo
description: Pasta-of-the-day and hand-rolled tagliatelle in an Islington dining room — Padella's big sister, run by the same team.
tips: £45 prix fixe for two courses. Pappardelle al ragu is a must.

name: Bancone
description: Counter pasta in Covent Garden — the silk-handkerchief pasta with walnut butter is one of the city's best Instagram dishes and is genuinely delicious.
tips: Silk handkerchief pasta with walnut butter is non-negotiable.

name: Duck & Waffle Local
description: The sit-down sibling of the 24-hour tower restaurant — a smarter St James's dining room with bar-forward menu.
tips: The original Duck & Waffle Tower offers the view; this one offers the food.

name: Murano
description: Angela Hartnett's Michelin-starred Mayfair Italian — refined, unfussy, and impeccably warm.
tips: Lunch tasting menu £50 — one of London's best fine-dining bargains.

name: Café Murano
description: Angela Hartnett's casual Italian wine bar and restaurant in St James's — the more accessible sister to Murano.
tips: Five branches across London. Set lunch £25.

name: San Carlo Cicchetti
description: Italian cichetti bar on Piccadilly — Venetian-style small plates, a glamorous theatre district spot.
tips: Pre-theatre menu excellent.

name: Pastaio
description: Affordable fresh pasta in Kingly Court — rolled and cut on-site, £7-12 bowls, casual counter-style.
tips: Walk-in-friendly. Bright, buzzy, great for solo dining.

name: Bonhams Restaurant
description: A Michelin-starred lunch-only restaurant inside the Mayfair auction house — tasting menu by chef Tom Kemble.
tips: Closed weekends. Lunch only.

name: Pied à Terre
description: London's longest-running Michelin-starred restaurant (1991) in Fitzrovia — fine dining without the fuss.
tips: Lunch set £49. Tasting menu £120.

name: Otto's French Restaurant
description: A tucked-away Bloomsbury legend — the only London restaurant still serving canard à la presse (pressed duck) tableside.
tips: Pressed duck must be ordered 24h ahead — for 2 people. Theatrical.

name: Galvin Bistrot de Luxe
description: Marylebone institution of classical French bistro cooking — cassoulet, confit de canard, pot-au-feu done perfectly.
tips: Pre-theatre £30 two-course menu excellent.

name: Les 110 de Taillevent
description: A Marylebone outpost of Paris institution Taillevent — 110 wines by the glass across four price tiers per dish.
tips: Wine flight paired with each course — a genuine wine education.

name: Pollen Street Social
description: Jason Atherton's flagship — Michelin-starred modern British in Mayfair. The open kitchen and dessert bar are both memorable.
tips: Chef's counter seats have the full kitchen view.

name: Brasserie Joel
description: British-French brasserie inside the Park Plaza Westminster Bridge — pleasing food, reliable service, river location.
tips: Pre-theatre menu convenient for National Theatre.

name: Pharmacy 2 by Damien Hirst
description: Damien Hirst's art-world restaurant at Newport Street Gallery — the original Pharmacy's much-loved successor.
tips: Combine with free gallery visit.

name: Scott's
description: Caprice Holdings' Mayfair institution — a legendary seafood and oyster restaurant in Mount Street.
tips: Ian Fleming used to dine here. Still celebrity-heavy.

name: The Ivy Covent Garden
description: The original Ivy, open since 1917 — the legendary theatre-district brasserie under the same roof as writers' club The Ivy Market Grill.
tips: Shepherd's pie and bread-and-butter pudding still on menu after 100+ years.

name: Balthazar London
description: Covent Garden outpost of Keith McNally's New York brasserie — zinc bar, French classics, huge brunch menu.
tips: Weekend brunch most popular — book 3 weeks ahead.

name: Kudu
description: South African-influenced small plates in Peckham — the carpet-braaied lamb neck is the signature of a young, exciting kitchen.
tips: Sister restaurant Kudu Grill next door for more meat-focused menu.

name: Sessions Arts Club
description: A former courtroom above the Old Sessions House in Clerkenwell — faded grandeur, candle-lit, a Florian-Nouveau interior.
tips: The Instagram-famous room is the draw. Book weeks ahead.

name: Cora Pearl
description: The younger sister to Kitty Fisher's — a relaxed Covent Garden restaurant serving refined comfort food with an exceptional wine list.
tips: The creamed cauliflower and mash with ham hock is house-defining.

name: Kitty Fisher's
description: A tiny, romantic Shepherd Market basement — wood-fired cooking, warm service, candle-lit tables.
tips: Named for an 18th-century courtesan. Book 3 weeks ahead.

name: Frenchie
description: A Paris restaurant's London outpost in Covent Garden — new-wave French bistronomie with Asian influences.
tips: The smoked haddock with Gorgonzola is a signature.

name: Medlar
description: Former Michelin-starred Chelsea neighbourhood restaurant — elegant French cooking, a secret gem of King's Road.
tips: Tasting menu £95; set lunch £40.

name: Oystermen
description: Tiny Seven Dials oyster bar — expert shuckers at a marble counter, plates of shrimp, and flights of English white wine.
tips: Dozen oysters and a bottle of English white — the perfect pre-theatre stop.

name: Wright Brothers Soho
description: A no-nonsense oyster bar and seafood kitchen on Kingly Street — marble counter, lobster rolls, champagnes by the glass.
tips: Happy hour oysters £1 each 3-6pm Mon-Fri. Borough Market original also great.

name: J Sheekey
description: St Martin's Court seafood institution since 1896 — a warren of wood-panelled rooms, Dover sole, and a faithful theatre-district following.
tips: The Oyster Bar next door takes walk-ins; the restaurant does not.

name: Little Social
description: Jason Atherton's bistro across Pollen Street from his flagship — warm, convivial, French-influenced.
tips: Set menu £35 excellent value.

name: Chiltern Firehouse
description: André Balazs's Marylebone celebrity-haunt — converted fire station, Nuno Mendes at the stoves, hard to book, easy to love.
tips: Book 28 days in advance at 9am. Crab doughnuts a signature.

name: Palomar Soho
description: The West End's pan-Mediterranean 20-seat counter — Tel Aviv meets Jerusalem, lively, loud, perfect fun.
tips: Open kitchen counter for the full show.

name: The Red Fort
description: Long-standing elegant Indian in Soho (1983) — named after the Mughal citadel, a spacious restaurant with a renowned Akbar basement bar.
tips: Pre-theatre menu £32.50.

name: Roti King
description: Malaysian-style roti canai counter in Euston — tiny, cash-friendly, with possibly London's most famous queue.
tips: Cash preferred. Walk-in only — expect 45+ minute queues.

name: Sambal Shiok Laksa Bar
description: Laksa specialists on Holloway Road — Penang-style coconut curry noodles, spicy prawn, and turmeric-rich broths.
tips: Extra sambal on request. Lunch busy with food-scene regulars.

name: Brilliant
description: Southall's legendary Punjabi restaurant since 1975 — Jeera chicken, butter chicken, tandoori platters beloved by generations.
tips: Close to Southall station (Elizabeth Line). Worth the journey for Jeera chicken.

name: Gifto's Lahore Karahi
description: A Southall institution for Punjabi cuisine — specialising in karahi (wok) dishes, tandoori, and naan straight from the clay oven.
tips: Cash-friendly. Vast menu.

name: Gökyüzü
description: Turkey meets Green Lanes — the biggest, buzziest of Harringay's Turkish meze-and-mangal restaurants.
tips: Complimentary bread and dips with every meal. Family-friendly.

name: Antepliler
description: Green Lanes Turkish restaurant focused on Gaziantep cuisine — the pistachio-land of Turkey, with sublime baklava.
tips: The baklava and katmer are imported recipes. Essential.

name: Roka Aldwych
description: Riverside Roka branch near the Strand — same robatayaki menu as the flagship, better for theatre-adjacent dining.
tips: Pre-theatre menu £33 — a relative bargain.

name: Tonkotsu Soho
description: London's first proper ramen specialist — the Tonkotsu flagship on Dean Street, with rich 18-hour pork-bone broth.
tips: Add kae-dama (extra noodles) for £2. Nine branches across London.

name: Kanada-Ya
description: Hakata-style tonkotsu ramen on St Giles — 18-hour broth, firm straight noodles, always a 30-minute queue.
address: 64 St Giles High St, London WC2H 8LE
tips: Walk-in only. Arrive before 12 for lunch.

name: Shoryu Ramen Regent Street
description: Kyushu-style tonkotsu ramen counter below the Japan Centre — reliable, fast, a good gateway ramen.
tips: Eight branches. Japanese whisky cocktails at the Regent Street upstairs bar.

name: Bone Daddies Soho
description: Rock'n'roll ramen with a late-night license — broths aren't strictly traditional, music is loud, food is fun.
tips: Open late. Kicking it Oldskool ramen is the classic.

name: Tokimeite Mayfair
description: Mayfair sister to Zuma — Japanese-Australian sushi, wagyu beef, and the quiet air of an insider's spot.
tips: Wagyu sushi is a marquee order.

name: Sakagura
description: Subterranean Japanese restaurant and izakaya near Heddon Street — exceptional sake list, 150+ premium bottles.
tips: Ask for a sake flight matched to your dish.

name: Sosharu
description: Jason Atherton's izakaya in Clerkenwell — Japanese tavern cooking, a central sushi counter, and a downstairs sake bar.
tips: Bar 7 Tales downstairs is a beautifully dark cocktail bar.

name: Sake no Hana
description: Alan Yau's St James's Japanese — a contemporary bamboo-latticed room, top-tier sushi and kaiseki.
tips: Set lunch £39.50.

name: Bibimbap Soho
description: Korean bibimbap specialist — sizzling stone bowls of rice, vegetables, bulgogi, a reliable Soho budget lunch.
tips: Lunch £10 with a drink — hard to beat.

name: Kimchee
description: Fast-casual Korean in Holborn — bibimbap, bulgogi, and fried-chicken bucket deals.
tips: Popular with the LSE crowd.

name: Yori Korean BBQ
description: Smoky Korean BBQ on Soho Street — tabletop grills, soju flights, and a lively karaoke vibe downstairs.
tips: Book ahead weekends. Karaoke rooms to reserve.

name: SushiSamba Covent Garden
description: The Covent Garden SushiSamba in the former Opera Tavern — Brazilian-Japanese hybrid at a more intimate scale than Heron Tower.
address: 35 The Market Covent Garden, London WC2E 8RF
tips: Bottomless brunch at weekends.

name: Darjeeling Express
description: Asma Khan's Indian restaurant in Garrick Street — an all-female kitchen serving hearty, genuinely home-style Indian food.
tips: Biryani thali is the signature. Feast menu great for groups.

name: Indian Accent
description: Mayfair outpost of Manish Mehrotra's New Delhi fine-dining Indian — modernist technique on Old India dishes.
tips: Paired tasting menus are exceptional.

name: Bibi
description: Chet Sharma's JKS-Group Mayfair restaurant — reinterpreting Indian subcontinent cooking through a fine-dining lens.
tips: Michelin-starred. Book 3-4 weeks ahead.

name: Soutine
description: Corbin & King's all-day brasserie in St John's Wood — the most Parisian-feeling restaurant north of the Thames.
address: 60 St John's Wood High St, London NW8 7SH
tips: Brunch here is a weekend tradition.

name: BRAT x Climpson's Arch
description: A summer-residency outdoor grill by BRAT's Tomos Parry — a 30-seater at Climpson's Arch railway arch in London Fields.
tips: Summer only. Book months ahead.

name: Mao Chow
description: Sichuan in Hackney — dan-dan noodles and spicy wontons, a tiny Kingsland Road favourite.
tips: Walk-in. Cash-preferred.

name: Xi'an Impression
description: A tiny Holloway Road café beside Arsenal's Emirates — hand-pulled biang-biang noodles, cumin lamb, pork and chilli burgers.
tips: Biang-biang noodles and pork burger essential.

name: Silk Road Camberwell
description: Uighur noodles and dumplings in a tiny Camberwell café — big plates of lamb, hand-stretched noodles, cash-preferred.
tips: Cash preferred. Walk-in-friendly.

name: Dumplings' Legend
description: Chinatown's Shanghai-style xiaolongbao specialist — soup dumplings made in the front window; a Gerrard Street classic.
tips: Soup dumplings the must-order. Walk-in crowd.

name: Cây Tre Soho
description: Vietnamese restaurant on Old Compton Street — pho, bún bò Huế, banh mi; perfect for late-night bowls.
tips: Open late. Pho ga is the classic choice.

name: Viet Food
description: Jeff Tan's loud, happy Vietnamese restaurant in Soho — big bowls, fish sauce cocktails, a Spinning Wheel of Fortune for free desserts.
tips: Open late. Bánh xèo pancakes are excellent.

name: Banh Mi Bay
description: Fresh Vietnamese banh mi on Theobald's Road — proper crusty baguettes, pâté, pickled carrot, chilli.
tips: BBQ pork banh mi a classic. Takeaway-friendly.

name: Song Que
description: Kingsland Road Vietnamese institution since 2001 — pho, bun bo hue, and the best banh xeo pancakes in Shoreditch.
tips: BYOB allowed. Part of the Kingsland Road 'Pho Mile' strip.

name: Mien Tay
description: Vietnamese Pho Mile restaurant specialising in southern and Mekong Delta cuisine — grilled seafood and claypot dishes.
tips: Grilled monk fish in turmeric is a speciality.

name: Kappacasein Dairy
description: A Bermondsey arch cheesemaker famed for its £9 raclette toastie and grilled cheese — one of London's true single-dish destinations.
tips: Open Saturdays only at Maltby Street Market. Expect a queue.

name: Monty's Deli
description: Fleet Street-reviving Jewish deli in Hoxton — pastrami sandwiches, matzo ball soup, pickled herring, cheesecake.
tips: Pastrami and rye is essential. Open into evenings.

name: Som Saa's Spitalfields Original
description: The Blue Posts upstairs restaurant in Soho — the Palomar team's 60-seater, with a theatre-kitchen view.
tips: Genuinely good value in the West End — book ahead.

name: Sabrage — English Sparkling Bar
description: West End champagne bar specialising in English sparkling wine — a free educational tasting comparison with Champagne.
tips: English sparkling flights £28. Food pairings available.

name: Swift Cocktails Soho
description: Two-floor drinking den on Old Compton Street — upstairs pre-dinner, downstairs speakeasy whiskey bar.
tips: Irish coffee a signature. 150+ whiskies downstairs.

name: Morgan M
description: Morgan Meunier's long-standing Clerkenwell French restaurant — classical, quiet, Michelin-star fine dining.
tips: Tasting menu pairs with French Burgundy.

name: Mere
description: Monica Galetti's Fitzrovia restaurant — contemporary European in a calm basement, the MasterChef professional's home kitchen.
tips: Three-course lunch £38.

name: Yauatcha City
description: The Square Mile branch of the all-day dim sum favourite — in a sleek Broadgate Circle space.
tips: Try the macarons downstairs — petit fours for the bar.

name: Lyaness
description: Mr Lyan's Sea Containers bar — world-class cocktails built on 'ingredients we make ourselves'.
tips: Tasting flights available. Food menu is snacks-only.

name: Blue Elephant
description: Royal Thai in Fulham's Imperial Wharf — opulent gilded setting, classic Thai menu, big on fruit carvings.
address: The Boulevard, Imperial Wharf, London SW6 2UB
tips: Sunday brunch champagne menu a weekend classic.

name: Restaurant Gordon Ramsay
description: Gordon Ramsay's three-Michelin-starred Chelsea flagship (1998) — the restaurant that launched his empire.
tips: Tasting menu £225. Dress code enforced. Jackets preferred.

name: Alain Ducasse at the Dorchester
description: Three Michelin stars inside the Dorchester — contemporary French haute cuisine with a private 'Table Lumière' booth.
tips: Book the Table Lumière — a booth inside a fibre-optic curtain.

name: Aquavit London
description: St James's Scandi-fine-dining restaurant — herring, pickled beetroot, venison, and an interior of pale woods and bright lamps.
address: St James's Market, 1 Carlton St, London SW1Y 4QQ
tips: Set lunch £29. Open daily.

name: Ekstedt at The Yard
description: Swedish fire-and-smoke cooking at the Great Scotland Yard Hotel — food cooked over birch, juniper and open coals, no electricity.
tips: Tasting menu only. Dinner from 6pm.

name: Hide Above
description: The Michelin-starred upper floor of Hide in Mayfair — modern British tasting menu with Green Park views.
tips: Ground-floor Hide & Seek is cheaper with same kitchen.

name: Borough Market Small-Plates Tour
description: A self-guided food tour of Borough Market stalls — the Bread Ahead doughnut, Kappacasein toastie, Ottolenghi, Brindisa tapas.
tips: Saturday is peak. Weekdays quieter. Go hungry.

name: Café Cecilia
description: Max Rocha's (son of John Rocha) airy canal-side restaurant in Hackney — simple, seasonal, and hugely in demand.
tips: Book weeks ahead. The buttermilk roast chicken for two is the signature.

name: Akoko
description: Fitzrovia West African restaurant — Michelin Bib Gourmand, tasting menu spans Sierra Leone, Nigeria, Ghana.
tips: Tasting menu only. Book weeks ahead.

name: Chishuru
description: Adejoke Bakare's Fitzrovia West African restaurant — a seasonal menu celebrating a pan-African pantry, Michelin-starred 2024.
tips: Tasting menu £65. First female African chef to win a Michelin star in the UK.

name: Yayah's — Golden Chippy
description: A legendary fish-and-chip-shop on Greenwich's Blackheath Road with a tuk-tuk on the roof — proper British chippy, Caribbean-accented.
tips: The cod fillet is massive. Jerk chicken dishes a cult pick.

name: Goddards at Greenwich
description: An East End-style pie-and-mash shop that has moved to Greenwich — proper jellied eels, meat pie, liquor, since 1890.
tips: Pie, mash, liquor, jellied eels all £8 each. Cash preferred.

name: M. Manze Pie and Mash
description: The oldest surviving pie-and-mash shop (1902) — Tower Bridge Road institution, tile-walled, Grade II-listed interior.
tips: Closes at 4pm. Cash only. Order pie + mash with liquor — the green parsley sauce is the secret.

name: Café OTO
description: Experimental-music café and venue in Dalston — gigs many nights, a daytime café, and a brilliantly curated record/book shop.
tips: Gig-only access in the evenings. Great record shop upstairs.

name: Tramshed
description: A Mark Hix restaurant in Shoreditch (now closed but iconic)
tips: Under redevelopment 2026 — check before visiting.

name: Popolo
description: Shoreditch pasta and small plates bar — Italian seasonal cooking, walk-in and counter-style, endlessly buzzy.
tips: Walk-ins at counter only; tables bookable.

name: Saint Leonards
description: A smart Shoreditch restaurant cooking over open fire and raw-bar seafood — a statement of modern-British ambition.
tips: Whole grilled fish is the signature move.

name: Rotorino
description: Stevie Parle's Dalston southern-Italian restaurant — handmade pasta, wood-oven pizza, and a lively bar.
tips: Sunday lunch excellent — bring friends.

name: Jolene
description: Jeremy Lee-style Newington Green restaurant and bakery — big windows, open kitchen, Parisian café feel.
tips: Bakery takeaway from 8am. Small daily menu.

name: Westerns Laundry
description: A sister to Primeur — industrial-chic Highbury corner restaurant serving immaculate seafood and natural wine.
tips: Whole fish special is always excellent.

name: Primeur
description: Canonbury corner restaurant serving small plates to share — natural wine, French-inflected cooking, lively atmosphere.
tips: Walk-in-friendly at counter. Book for tables.

name: Planque
description: Kingsland Road restaurant and wine club — industrial setting, immaculate small-plates, serious wine cellar.
tips: Cellar membership gives access to rare-vintage offers.

name: Forza Wine
description: A Peckham rooftop wine bar and restaurant — natural wines and Italian small plates, sunset views.
tips: Arrive early for sunset — Thursday is packed.

name: Levan
description: A Peckham natural-wine restaurant — sister to Forza Wine with more substantial plates and a big open kitchen.
tips: Open late. Try the natural fizz.

name: Peg
description: Jonathan Lawson's Hackney yakitori and natural-wine bar — hot counter seats overlooking the grill.
tips: Sister restaurant Legs a block away.

name: Legs
description: Hackney's Broadway Market restaurant — small plates, Italian-leaning, a big wine list.
tips: Pasta changes daily. The pici is always excellent.

name: Lahpet
description: Burmese restaurant in Shoreditch — tea-leaf salad, fish-curry mohinga, a lively bar scene.
tips: Tea-leaf salad is the house signature.

name: Zia Lucia
description: Islington pizzeria with a 48-hour dough and an ink-black charcoal crust — a new-wave London pizza classic.
tips: Charcoal dough is the signature. 10 branches now.

name: Pizza Pilgrims Dean St
description: Soho's beloved Neapolitan pizzeria — brothers James and Thom Elliott opened their first bricks-and-mortar here in 2013.
tips: Lots of branches. Margherita classic; Nutella pizza ring the closer.

name: Franco Manca Brixton
description: The original Franco Manca in Brixton Market — sourdough Neapolitan pizza for under £10, now a household name.
tips: Walk-in only. Lunch queues move fast.

name: Ace Pizza London Fields
description: Tom Kerridge's pizzeria on the edge of London Fields — sourdough Neapolitan, a strong natural wine list.
tips: Book or walk-in. 'Ace' pizza is a must try.

name: Burger & Lobster Mayfair
description: Single-concept cult restaurant — choose a burger, lobster, or lobster roll for £26. Five locations; Mayfair is the original.
tips: Walk-in. Lobster roll is the pick.

name: Patty & Bun Soho
description: Smashed burger specialist on James Street — the Ari Gold burger with smoky mayo has a cult following.
tips: Queue or walk-in. 10+ branches across London.

name: Shake Shack Covent Garden
description: The original UK Shake Shack in Covent Garden's Piazza — reliable smashburgers, crinkle fries, and concretes.
tips: Al fresco seating in the Piazza is lovely.

name: Bleecker Burger
description: New York-style smashburger joint with multiple central branches — short menu, thin patties, no frills, pure craft.
tips: Cheeseburger and black and blue burger are the picks.

name: Supawan
description: Thai family restaurant in King's Cross — neighbourhood classic with genuine regional dishes like khao soi and boat noodles.
tips: Northern-Thai menu; khao soi is the must-order.
